mainTopic: Checking the lung: a hole in only one layer, רב יוסף's air test, and רבא's rulings on peeled, reddened, dried, scabbed and stuck-together lungs.
overview: This amud is about checking an animal's lung to see if it is a טרפה. First it finishes רבא's ruling that a lung whose outer layer peeled off, leaving it red like a date, is כשרה. Next it asks what happens if only the inner layer of the lung has a hole. רב אחא and רבינא disagree, and the הלכה is that the outer layer protects. The proof is רב יוסף's test with a feather, saliva, straw or lukewarm water: if no air escapes, the sound is just air between the layers. After a memory aid (סימן), the גמרא goes through a series of רבא's rulings. For a reddened lung, רבינא shows there is no real difference between part and all. A partly dried lung is a טרפה only if it crumbles under a fingernail, and the גמרא shows even the רבנן can agree to this. Scabs and dark spots are כשרה, cysts may not be compared to each other, and two lobes stuck together out of their natural order make the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: Finishing the ruling: a peeled lung that looks like a red date is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier ruling: a lung whose outer layer peeled off, leaving it like a red date, is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it looks like a red date, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence of רבא that started just before this. A lung whose outer layer peeled off, so that it looks like a red date, is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the outer layer, so that the red lung underneath shows, does not make the animal a טרפה. This closes the earlier discussion so the גמרא can move on to a new question about holes in the lung's layers.

phrases.english: Like a red date – it is kosher.
phrases.notes: This finishes a ruling of רבא from just before: a lung whose outer layer peeled off and looks like this is still kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung whose outer layer peeled off, leaving it red like a date, is כשרה.

steps.title: Inner layer pierced, outer layer whole: does it protect?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if only the inner layer of the lung has a hole and the outer layer is whole, does the outer layer save the animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the inner layer was pierced but the outer layer was not pierced, does the outer layer protect, or does it not protect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a lung with two layers, where only the inner one has a hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole that goes all the way through the lung makes the animal a טרפה. The question is whether one whole outer layer is enough to count the lung as 'closed', or whether a hole in either layer is already a problem.

phrases.english: If the lower one was pierced and the upper one was not pierced –
phrases.notes: The lung has two layers. The 'lower' one is the inner layer and the 'upper' one is the outer layer.

phrases.english: does it protect, or does it not protect?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the previous ruling closes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an outer layer that is whole saves a lung whose inner layer has a hole.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue about the question. One says the outer layer does not protect, and the other says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says it does not protect, and one says it does protect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that the question is a disagreement between רב אחא and רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are not told which sage holds which view. The answer to the question is a dispute, so the גמרא still needs to tell us how the הלכה goes.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it:
one says: it does not protect,
and one says: it protects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by presenting a dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are two views: it protects, or it does not protect.

steps.title: The הלכה: the outer layer protects
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows the view that the outer layer protects, in line with רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is that it protects, in line with רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the dispute: the outer layer protects, so the animal is כשרה. It is setting up a proof from רב יוסף, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is backed by an earlier statement of רב יוסף. His statement does not discuss this question directly, but his test for a lung only works if a hole in the inner layer alone does not make the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with רב יוסף's view

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, if only the inner layer has a hole and the outer layer is whole, the animal is כשרה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is that it protects, in line with Rav Yosef,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute from the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The outer layer protects; the animal is כשרה.

steps.title: רב יוסף's test when we know where the sound comes from
steps.stepSummary: For a lung that hisses, if we know the spot, we put a feather, saliva or straw there. If it bubbles it is a טרפה; if not, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף said: a lung that makes a sound, if we know where it makes the sound, we put on it a feather, saliva or straw. If it bubbles, it is a טרפה; if not, it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב יוסף's test as the source for the ruling. When the lung is blown up and hisses at a known spot, we check whether air really escapes there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sound shows that something is wrong inside the lung. Only air coming out through the outer surface makes it a טרפה. If the feather, saliva or straw shows no air escaping, the animal is כשרה even though there was a sound.

keyTerms.meaning: That makes a noise or hiss
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הַאי רֵיאָה דְּאָוְושָׁא,
phrases.english: As Rav Yosef said: this lung that makes a sound,
if we know where it makes the sound –

phrases.aramaic: מוֹתְבִינַן עֲלַהּ גַּדְפָּא אוֹ רוּקָּא אוֹ גִילָא,
phrases.english: we put on it a feather, or saliva, or a straw;
if it bubbles – it is a tereifa,
and if not – it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הַאי רֵיאָה דְּאָוְושָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source quoted for the ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That an inner hole alone does not make the animal a טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's test for a hissing lung.

steps.title: If we don't know where the sound comes from: use a basin of water
steps.stepSummary: If the spot is unknown, we put the lung in a basin of lukewarm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we don't know where it makes the sound, we bring a basin of lukewarm water and put the lung inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second method for when we can't find the spot of the sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water shows bubbles from any spot on the lung, so it finds a hole even when we don't know where it is. The next step explains why the water must be lukewarm.

phrases.english: And if we don't know where it makes the sound –
we bring a basin of lukewarm water
and put it inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's statement with the case where the spot is unknown.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the spot of the sound is unknown, check the lung in lukewarm water.

steps.title: Why lukewarm water, not hot or cold
steps.stepSummary: Hot water makes the lung shrink, and cold water makes it hard. So we use lukewarm water and blow the lung up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not in hot water, because it makes the lung shrink. Not in cold water, because it makes it hard. Rather, we put it in lukewarm water and blow it up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why the water has to be lukewarm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot water would shrink the lung and could close up a real hole, so we would wrongly call it כשרה. Cold water would stiffen the lung. Lukewarm water avoids both problems, so the test is fair.

phrases.english: Not in hot water – because it makes it shrink,
phrases.notes: Shrinking could close up a real hole and hide it.

phrases.english: not in cold water – because it makes it hard,
rather, we put it in lukewarm water and blow it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the water in the previous step is lukewarm.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The test uses lukewarm water, not hot or cold.

steps.title: No bubbles means kosher: the sound is air between the layers
steps.stepSummary: If it bubbles it is a טרפה; if not, it is כשרה. The inner layer has a hole but the outer one does not, and the sound is air between the layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it bubbles, it is a טרפה; if not, it is כשרה. The inner layer was pierced, the outer layer was not, and the sound is just air between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the result of the water test and explains it. This is exactly the proof the גמרא needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lung that hisses but does not bubble must have a hole only in the inner layer, with air moving between the two layers. רב יוסף calls it כשרה, so he holds that the outer layer protects. That is why the הלכה follows the view that it protects.

keyTerms.meaning: That is in between (the two layers)

steps.whatToRemember: A hissing lung with no air escaping outside is כשרה. The sound comes from air between the layers, which proves the outer layer protects.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the sound by itself makes the animal a טרפה. Only air escaping through the outer layer, shown by bubbles, does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical basis for checking lungs: the outer layer decides whether the animal is a טרפה.

phrases.english: If it bubbles – it is a tereifa,
and if not – it is kosher;
the inner one was pierced, the outer one was not pierced,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי דְּאָוְושָׁא – זִיקָא דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי הוּא.
phrases.english: and the fact that it makes a sound – it is air in between.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the water test and shows how it proves the הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An inner hole alone does not make the animal a טרפה, because the outer layer protects.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next rulings
steps.stepSummary: A סימן (memory aid) of key words for the rulings about the lung that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Dates, red, that dried, scabs – a memory aid.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the next group of rulings. It is setting up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one upcoming ruling about the lung. It is not a ruling by itself; it is just a tool for remembering the order.

phrases.english: (Dates, red, that dried, scabs – a memory aid).
phrases.notes: Each word hints at one of the coming rulings about the lung, in order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition that introduces the next set of rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for the rulings that follow.

steps.title: A peeled lung that looks like a red date is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבא's statement that a lung whose outer layer peeled off, leaving it looking like a red date, is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: רבא said, a lung whose outer layer peeled off so it looks like a red date is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement of רבא that was mentioned earlier and now discusses it on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lung has an outer layer. If that layer came off and the lung underneath looks red like a date, רבא says the animal is still כשרה. This opens a short series of רבא's rulings about the lung.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself'. The גמרא returns to a statement it quoted earlier.
Was peeled. The outer layer came off.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rava said:
This lung that was peeled
like a red date is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the סימן in step 9, returning to an earlier statement of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lung whose outer layer peeled off, leaving it red like a date, is כשרה.

steps.title: A lung that turned red: part is kosher, all is not
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if part of a lung turned red it is כשרה, but if the whole lung turned red it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: a lung that turned red in part is kosher; if all of it turned red, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second ruling. Here the lung is red from bleeding, and he splits between part of the lung and all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא draws a line based on how much of the lung turned red. A small red area is fine, but a fully red lung makes the animal a טרפה. The next step will challenge why there should be any difference.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A lung that turned red in part is kosher;
all of it, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבא about the lung's color.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partial reddening is כשרה, full reddening is טרפה.

steps.title: רבינא: if part heals, the whole should heal too
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא: part of the lung is כשרה because it heals, but a fully red lung also heals, as a ברייתא shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: why is part kosher? Because it heals. Then all of it also heals! Isn't it taught: for other creeping creatures, one is not liable until blood comes out of them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רבא's split between part and all. He argues that redness heals either way, and he brings a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumes partial redness is כשרה because the animal recovers. He then cites a ברייתא about wounding creatures on שבת: for most creatures you are only liable once blood actually comes out. That means blood trapped under the skin, which just looks red, goes back and heals, so a fully red lung should heal too.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes back to being healthy. It heals.
Until blood comes out of them

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Part of it, what is the reason?
Because it heals again;
all of it also heals again!
Isn't it taught in a baraita:
And other repulsive creatures and creeping animals,
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is about wounding creatures on שבת. For these other creatures you aren't liable just for a bruise.

phrases.english: not until blood comes out of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: מִקְצָתָהּ מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction between partial and full reddening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If partial redness is כשרה because it heals, the ברייתא shows that trapped blood heals in general, so full redness should heal too.

steps.title: Suggested answer: compare the lung to the eight שרצים
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests a possible answer: maybe the lung is like the eight שרצים, where trapped blood counts even if it does not come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: we compare the lung to the eight שרצים, as it is taught: if the blood collected, even though it did not come out, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a possible way to defend רבא. He is setting this answer up only so he can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the eight שרצים listed in the תורה, blood trapped under the skin counts as a lasting wound, because it does not go back. If the lung were like them, redness would be a lasting wound and could make the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It introduces a possible answer.
The eight creeping creatures listed in the תורה
The blood collected under the skin

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבינא's real view. It is a suggested answer that he will reject right away in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
we compare it to the eight creeping creatures,
as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: נִצְרַר הַדָּם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא.
phrases.english: if the blood collected, even though it did not come out.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא means he is liable for wounding one of the eight שרצים once blood gathers under the skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לִשְׁמוֹנָה שְׁרָצִים מְדַמֵּינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of רבא against the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing the lung to a different category, the eight שרצים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Redness in a lung, like trapped blood in the eight שרצים, does not heal.

steps.title: Then even part should be a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the suggestion: if trapped blood never heals, even a partly red lung should be a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even part of it too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא knocks down the suggested answer from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lung is like the eight שרצים and its redness never heals, the split still fails. Then even partial redness should make the animal a טרפה. Either way, part and whole should be treated the same.

phrases.english: If so,
even part of it as well!
phrases.notes: He means even partial redness should make it a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison to the eight שרצים as a way to save רבא's split
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It proves too much. It would make partial redness a טרפה too.

steps.title: No difference between part and all
steps.stepSummary: רבינא concludes that partial and full reddening must be treated the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge ends with the conclusion that רבא's split between part and all does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to the eight שרצים was rejected in step 14. What is left is רבינא's proof from the ברייתא that trapped blood heals. So part and whole share one ruling: even a lung that turned fully red is כשרה, and רבא's split between part and all is dropped.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא split partial redness, which is כשרה, from full redness, which is טרפה. רבינא showed that no reason supports the split. Since redness heals, part and all are the same: both are כשרה.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.
phrases.notes: No difference between a lung that is partly red and one that is fully red.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the challenge from steps 12 to 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Partial and full reddening of the lung are treated the same.

steps.title: A partly dried lung is a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if even part of a lung dried up, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: a lung that dried up in part is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of רבא, this time about a lung that has dried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike redness, dryness makes the animal a טרפה even if only part of the lung is affected. The next step asks how dry it has to be.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A lung that dried up in part is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling of רבא about the lung, after the reddening discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even partial drying of the lung makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: How dry must it be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how dry the lung must be to make the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a measure of the dryness in רבא's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Dried" could mean a little dry or very dry, so the גמרא wants a clear standard.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: He means how dry the lung has to be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure in step 16's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The degree of dryness that makes the lung a טרפה

steps.title: Dry enough to crumble with a fingernail
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, quoting רבא, says the lung must be dry enough to crumble with a fingernail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: enough that it can be crumbled with a fingernail.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי answers the question by giving רבא's measure for dryness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is practical. If the dry part crumbles when you press it with a fingernail, it counts as dried and the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whatToRemember: A partly dried lung is a טרפה if the dry part crumbles under a fingernail.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
enough that it crumbles with a fingernail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: כְּדַי שֶׁתִּפָּרֵךְ בְּצִפּוֹרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dry enough to crumble with a fingernail.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the fingernail rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבא's fingernail rule follows only רבי יוסי בן המשולם, who uses that same measure for a dried ear of a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Is it רבי יוסי בן המשולם's? A ברייתא teaches: what counts as a 'dried' ear? One that does not bleed even a drop when pierced. רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: it must be dry enough to crumble with a fingernail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רבא's fingernail measure from Step 18 sounds exactly like רבי יוסי בן המשולם's opinion about a dried ear. It asks whether רבא is following only that one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two measures of 'dry': the רבנן say it is dry if it does not bleed when pierced, and רבי יוסי בן המשולם says it must crumble with a fingernail. רבא used the fingernail measure, which demands much more dryness. So it looks like he follows the lone opinion rather than the majority. The question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? (Whose opinion does this follow?)

phrases.english: Whose view is this? Is it like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam?
phrases.notes: 'This' means רבא's rule from Step 18, that the lung must crumble with a fingernail.

phrases.english: As it is taught: What counts as a dried one?
phrases.notes: This is about the dried ear of a firstborn animal, a blemish that lets it be slaughtered outside the Temple.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם תִּינָּקֵב וְאֵינָהּ מוֹצִיאָה טִיפַּת דָּם;
phrases.english: One that, if pierced, does not let out a drop of blood.
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
It must be dry enough to crumble with a fingernail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the fingernail measure from Step 18 follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבא's fingernail measure follow only the lone view of רבי יוסי בן המשולם, against the רבנן?
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's fingernail measure for a dried lung
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same measure appears as a lone opinion against the רבנן, so רבא would seem to follow the minority view.

steps.title: Even the רבנן can agree, because a lung can heal
steps.stepSummary: An ear is exposed to wind and does not heal, but a lung is protected from air and can heal. So even the רבנן would require fingernail-level dryness for a lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן. An ear of a בכור is exposed to the wind, so it does not heal. But a lung is not exposed to the air, so it can heal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא does not have to follow only רבי יוסי בן המשולם. Even the רבנן would agree when it comes to a lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's easier measure (no blood) works for an ear because wind keeps drying it, so it will never recover. A lung sits inside the body, away from the air, so it may still heal unless it is so dry that it crumbles. The two cases are different, so there is no argument here.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the Sages (the majority)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single word, 'dry', can have a different measure depending on whether the body part is able to heal.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis.
Regarding the ear of a firstborn,
which the wind has power over,
it does not go back to health.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל רֵיאָה דְּלָא קָא שָׁלֵיט בַּהּ אַוֵּירָא –
phrases.english: But a lung, which the air has no power over,
does go back to health.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (ear compared with lung)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא must be following the lone opinion of רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן agree for a lung, because a lung is protected from air and can heal unless it crumbles.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fingernail measure fits the רבנן too, because of the difference between an exposed ear and a protected lung.

steps.title: A lung full of scabs or marks is still kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a lung covered with scabs, black spots, or patches of different colors is still כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a lung that is full of scabs, full of black spots, or full of patches of different appearances is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling: marks and scabs on the surface of a lung do not make the animal a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After all the talk about lung damage, רבא makes clear that not every strange-looking lung is a problem. Scabs, dark spots, and odd-colored patches alone do not make it a טרפה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the dried lung of Step 16. A dried-out lung is a טרפה, but surface marks and scabs are not.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
This lung that is
full of scabs, full of black spots,
or full of different-looking patches, is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling of רבא about the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scabs, black spots, or odd-colored patches on a lung do not make the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: You may not compare cysts on the lung
steps.stepSummary: אמימר, quoting רבא, rules that you may not compare one cyst on the lung to another to find out when it was pierced.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רבא: we do not compare cysts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: if a cyst on the lung is found pierced, you cannot pierce another cyst and compare the two to decide whether the first was pierced before or after the שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a test could show whether the hole is new, by making a fresh hole and seeing if it looks the same. רבא says this kind of comparison is not trusted for cysts.

keyTerms.meaning: Cysts or blisters on the lung

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rava:
We do not compare cysts.
phrases.notes: He means: you can't make a new hole in another cyst and match it to the pierced one to judge when the first hole was made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate ruling of רבא about the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A comparison test with another cyst may not be used to judge a pierced cyst.

steps.title: Two lobes stuck together cannot be checked
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that two lobes of the lung stuck to each other have no check that can save them, so the animal is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: two lobes that are stuck to each other cannot be saved by any check.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another rule: when two lobes of the lung are stuck together, we do not check them. The animal is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a problem on the lung can sometimes be checked and cleared. Here רבא says no check helps, because the sticking shows there was a hole in the lung.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: And Rava said:
These two lobes
that are stuck to each other
have no check.
phrases.notes: No check can make them kosher; the animal is a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling of רבא about lobes of the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two lobes stuck together make the animal a טרפה, with no check that can save it.

steps.title: Only lobes out of their natural order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבא's rule: it applies only when the lobes stuck together are not next to each other in their natural order. Lobes stuck in their order are just growing normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when they are out of order. But if they are in their order, that is simply how they grow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule from Step 23. It applies only to lobes that are stuck together out of their natural order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a lobe is stuck to the lobe right next to it, that is normal growth and the animal is כשרה. Only when a lobe sticks to one that is not its neighbor is it a sign of a hole, so the animal is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (limits a rule)
Not in their order (not neighboring lobes)

steps.whatToRemember: Lobes stuck together out of order make the animal a טרפה with no check. Neighboring lobes stuck together are normal and the animal is כשרה.

phrases.english: And we said this only when they are not in their order,
phrases.notes: Out of order means a lobe is stuck to a lobe that is not its neighbor.

phrases.english: but when they are in their order,
that is just how they grow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טרפה rule for stuck lobes applies only when they are out of their natural order; neighboring lobes stuck together are normal.
